title: Enterprise agent and autonomy registry
thesis: Create the system of record for every agent, bot, autonomous workflow, owner, purpose, deployment, interface, model, tool, data class, authority profile, and lifecycle state. The registry is the join point between technical identity and business accountability.
workflow: Discover from manifests, gateways, CI, cloud, and owner submissions
Deduplicate technical instances into governed agent versions
Assign accountable owner, use case, consequence, and lifecycle
Require signed change review when material fields change
metrics: share of active agents with verified manifests
risks: shadow agents remain unseen—compare passive discovery with owner declarations
registry becomes shelfware—tie authorization and evidence to registration
owner is nominal—require periodic attestation and escalation

title: Shadow-agent and autonomous-work discovery
thesis: Continuously identify likely agentic workloads, MCP clients and servers, service identities, scheduled automations, browser/computer-use sessions, and unregistered model/tool activity without claiming classification certainty.
workflow: Collect signals from identity, network, endpoint, cloud, CI, model gateway, and SaaS logs
Score likely autonomous behavior with evidence and confidence
Route candidates to an owner for confirm, dismiss, or investigate
Create or link the governed registry record
risks: employee surveillance—minimize and purpose-bind signals
false positives create distrust—show why and require human confirmation
detection is called control—label discovery as observation

title: Use-case, consequence, and autonomy classification
thesis: Classify the governed work unit—not only the model—by side effects, affected people, reversibility, data sensitivity, autonomy duration, delegation depth, external exposure, financial scope, and physical consequence.
workflow: Describe business purpose and expected effect
Apply deterministic classification rules and regional overlays
Show the factors and unresolved facts
Have the accountable owner sign the final classification
risks: single score hides consequence—retain factor vector
legal conclusion automated—require counsel/owner decision where applicable
teams under-classify to reduce friction—monitor overrides and incident outcomes

title: Agent lifecycle, dormancy, and retirement
outcome: Lower control debt and attack surface
thesis: Govern introduction, pilot, production, material change, suspension, dormancy, and retirement with expiry by default, evidence retention, credential revocation, connector removal, and successor mapping.
workflow: Set lifecycle and reauthorization dates
Detect inactivity, unsupported versions, ownership loss, or unresolved risk
Notify and suspend within policy
Retire identity, authority, secrets, routes, and deployment while preserving evidence
risks: automatic retirement breaks business work—stage and route exceptions
evidence is deleted with runtime—separate lifecycle from custody
ownership changes silently—bind HR/IdP events to review

title: Outcome contract and baseline
thesis: Require each governed use case to define the unit of work, intended business outcome, quality bar, deadline, full-cost boundary, acceptance owner, negative outcomes, and baseline before production claims begin.
workflow: Select or define outcome unit
Record pre-Warrantor baseline and measurement window
Name acceptance and attribution method
Approve counter-metrics and refresh cadence
risks: baseline selected after results—freeze prospectively
easy-to-measure proxy replaces outcome—require owner acceptance
hidden labor excluded—define full-cost boundary

title: Outcome attestation and acceptance
thesis: Link the post-commit technical outcome to a business acceptance event: what became real, whether it met quality and timing criteria, who accepted it, and what rework or harm followed.
workflow: Ingest technical completion from W2
Collect downstream result and quality evidence
Route to the named acceptance owner
Record accept, reject, partial, disputed, or expired with reason
metrics: share of completed work with linked outcome
risks: acceptance rubber-stamped—sample and measure reversals
technical success mistaken for business value—keep states separate
sensitive business results leak—store reference and scoped projection

title: Total-cost and resource attribution
thesis: Attribute model tokens, tools, GPUs, cloud, licenses, retries, waiting, reviewer time, failed work, and support effort to the governed work unit and accepted outcome.
workflow: Capture cost events with work-unit and tenant identifiers
Normalize rates and shared costs
Allocate reviewer and platform overhead by declared method
Reconcile estimate with invoices and accepted outcomes
risks: false precision—show confidence and allocation method
optimizing cost degrades quality—pair quality counter-metrics
review labor becomes surveillance—aggregate and purpose-limit

title: Autonomy portfolio and investment decisions
thesis: Give leaders an evidence-backed portfolio of use cases showing adoption, autonomy, oversight, quality, risk, cost, realized outcome, and control debt, with explicit expand, narrow, pause, or retire decisions.
workflow: Aggregate governed work by owner, domain, outcome, and consequence
Compare against the agreed baseline and counter-metrics
Surface uncertainty, incidents, and control debt
Record investment decision and expected next proof
risks: ranking games metrics—use multi-dimensional view
correlation called causation—state attribution limits
high-risk work starved despite value—include strategic and mission criteria

title: Warrant-template and control-pattern library
thesis: Package reusable business intents, capability bounds, side-effect classes, approvals, context rights, egress, budgets, evidence, safe states, and success criteria as parameterized patterns rather than copied warrants.
workflow: Select a reference pattern by outcome and consequence
Bind environment-specific resources and owners
Run conflict and overbreadth checks
Approve, version, publish, and monitor reuse
risks: template cargo cult—show applicability conditions
shared template silently widens—material changes require reapproval
too many patterns—merge by outcome and retire unused

title: Plain-language scope and consequence preview
thesis: Translate a warrant into concrete examples of what the agent can, cannot, and may only request—while preserving the exact underlying resources, constraints, enforcement posture, and unresolved bypasses.
workflow: Render effective capability after delegation intersection
Group by data, tool, destination, spend, time, and side effect
Show representative allowed/refused scenarios and enforcement strength
Require reviewer acknowledgment of critical gaps
risks: natural language drifts from policy—bind to digest and generated tests
examples imply exhaustive coverage—state limitations
oversimplification hides dependency effects—link graph

title: Preflight simulation and consequence rehearsal
thesis: Execute a proposed manifest, warrant, policy, connector, and workflow against synthetic and replayed scenarios to reveal expected denies, approvals, egress, costs, dependencies, and safe-state behavior before authorization.
workflow: Select representative and adversarial scenarios
Run in non-committing shadow/staging topology
Compare expected with observed policy and connector behavior
Resolve discrepancies or accept residual risk
risks: simulation is called proof of production—label topology
synthetic scenarios miss real behavior—replay sanitized traces
unsafe external side effect—hard non-commit boundary

title: Purpose, time, consequence, and resource budget service
thesis: Unify scattered tool, path, egress, token, spend, time, execution-count, data-purpose, delegation, and side-effect constraints into one explainable budget model without changing the W1/W6 decision semantics.
workflow: Define budgets at organization, template, warrant, and sub-warrant levels
Compute the narrowest effective constraint
Reserve and consume with idempotency
Alert, deny, or route approval according to consequence
risks: separate budgets conflict—one precedence model
race or retry double-spends—atomic idempotent reservation
budget becomes business approval—keep authority and finance semantics explicit

title: Human, workload, device, and tenant identity binding
thesis: Bind every governed action to an accountable human or autonomous principal, attested workload identity, tenant, device/session where applicable, and current authorization—without rebuilding enterprise IAM or workload identity.
workflow: Federate human identity from enterprise IdP
Attest workload with SPIFFE/SPIRE or supported platform identity
Bind delegated chain and device/session to the warrant
Re-evaluate identity and revocation at consequential commit
risks: Warrantor becomes IdP—adopt instead
shared service account hides human—require accountable principal
device binding creates privacy risk—scope to consequential approvals

title: Multi-agent delegation graph and union-trap visualizer
thesis: Make effective authority across manager, planner, worker, specialist, and tool agents visible; explain where constraints narrow, conflict, expire, or become bottom; and detect sibling or fan-in attempts to combine authority.
workflow: Assemble heterogeneous token and warrant links
Recompute intersection at each edge
Render effective capability and lost constraints
Block or escalate union, cycle, impersonation, or unknown-constraint cases
risks: visual graph differs from verifier—derive from same canonical result
complexity overwhelms reviewer—progressive disclosure
graph exposes sensitive org structure—least-privilege projections

title: Just-in-time sub-warrants and authority leasing
thesis: Let a parent agent request a short-lived, task-specific sub-warrant whose authority is the intersection of parent scope, template policy, task need, and approver limit, with execution-count and release-consistency bounds.
workflow: Agent declares task and requested capability
System computes maximum lawful subset and risk
Auto-issue within pre-approved pattern or route approval
Expire/revoke and bind all child evidence to the chain
risks: task text manipulates scope—rules compute authority
lease outlives business need—short expiry and completion revoke
approval fragmentation—aggregate related low-risk requests

title: Bounded revocation and cross-domain authority federation
thesis: Provide measured revocation guarantees across caches, regions, disconnected edges, and partner trust domains using execution-count and release-consistency semantics rather than relying only on token TTL.
workflow: Declare revocation class and maximum propagation/usage
Distribute signed event across trust domains
Invalidate affected chain results and leases
Measure achieved latency and reconcile disconnected nodes
risks: guarantee impossible under partition—state mode and exposure
federation expands trust root—domain policy and blast caps
clock reliance—use counters and monotonic evidence where possible

title: Policy and control registry
thesis: Create a versioned registry linking business requirement, technical policy source, compiled targets, owner, tests, evidence fields, exceptions, applicability, jurisdiction, SLO, and retirement state.
workflow: Author or import control intent
Link policy source and target projections
Assign tests, evidence, owner, and review date
Approve version and monitor effectiveness
risks: registry duplicates GRC—focus on executable/evidenced controls
control exists without enforcement—show target/posture
jurisdiction content goes stale—version and owner

title: Policy workbench, semantic diff, and conflict analysis
thesis: Let policy authors review meaning, affected capabilities, target projections, conflicts, exceptions, expected denies, blast radius, and rollback—not only source-code text differences.
workflow: Edit human-readable intent and structured constraints
Compile to semantic intermediate form
Compare effective behavior and run scenarios
Approve staged rollout with rollback trigger
risks: AI-generated explanation is trusted—derive facts and label summaries
diff misses target behavior—differential tests
large blast radius—canary and shadow

title: Gateway/kernel equivalence laboratory
thesis: Continuously prove that semantic policy and conservative structural enforcement targets agree in the required direction across representative and adversarial actions, environments, and target versions.
workflow: Generate action/resource/constraint corpus
Compile to gateway and kernel targets
Evaluate both plus reference interpreter
Reject widening, quantify over-denial, and publish signed report
risks: equivalence claim exceeds corpus—state coverage
targets change semantics—version matrix
conservative denial causes outage—false-denial budget and staged rollout

title: Jurisdiction and sector control modules
thesis: Represent external obligations as versioned applicability questions, control intent, evidence needs, retention/residency constraints, and reporting views that compile through the same W4 model without embedding legal conclusions in core code.
workflow: Select official source and applicability scope
Map obligation to technical/operational facts
Review with local counsel and control owners
Publish signed version with update and deprecation policy
risks: module sold as legal compliance—evidence-only language
framework update lags—expiry and source monitoring
core forks per region—module contract

title: Unified risk-ordered decision inbox
thesis: Combine staged effects, policy exceptions, sub-warrants, connector discoveries, incidents, and evidence gaps into one queue ordered by consequence, expiry, dependency, business deadline, and reviewer authority.
workflow: Ingest decision request with canonical consequence and dependencies
Route by authority, SoD, availability, and SLA
Present changed facts, evidence, and allowed decisions
Record signed outcome, reason, and next dependency
risks: risk score hides urgency—show factors
queue overload causes rubber stamp—limits and sampling
wrong reviewer—cryptographic authority check at action

title: Dependency-aware partial approval and release
thesis: Allow a reviewer to release an independent subset of staged effects while preserving dependency order, effective authority, idempotency, and an exact record of what became real versus remained held or voided.
workflow: Build effect dependency DAG
Mark independent and coupled groups
Preview external consequences and authority for selected subset
Execute approved nodes in order and stop on failure boundary
risks: hidden dependency causes invalid release—explicit adapter-declared and inferred edges
compensation assumed—report rather than pretend undo
UI selection error—consequence preview and confirmation

title: Omnichannel notification, escalation, and mobile approval
thesis: Route actionable, signed, least-data decision notifications to web, desktop, mobile, email, chat, and incident channels with deep links, escalation, quiet hours, substitution, and offline-safe behavior.
workflow: Apply routing policy and channel sensitivity
Send minimal notification with signed request reference
Authenticate and re-fetch current decision state
Escalate, substitute, expire, or auto-hold according to policy
risks: approval from stale notification—re-fetch and re-evaluate
data leaks in channel—minimal content
fatigue—bundling, quiet hours, risk routing

title: Segregation of duties, quorum, and delegated approval
thesis: Support maker-checker, two-person, threshold, cross-function, jurisdictional, and emergency approval policies with non-delegable human steps and explicit conflict-of-interest constraints.
workflow: Compute required roles/quorum from consequence and policy
Resolve eligible principals and conflicts
Collect independent signed decisions
Re-evaluate quorum and current policy at commit
risks: delegation defeats non-delegable role—explicit flag
approval deadlock—substitute and SLA policy
quorum theater—independence and conflict evidence

title: Per-action enforcement posture and bypass map
thesis: Compute and display whether each resource/action class is enforced, mediated, observed, unsupported, or unknown based on attested deployment facts, connector coverage, and escape-suite freshness—not user configuration labels.
workflow: Collect topology and connector attestations
Map actions to mediation/enforcement path
Validate with escape tests and supported-version evidence
Downgrade on drift, expiry, or unknown path
risks: configured becomes claimed—require attestation
single global green hides action differences—per-class result
stale tests—expiry and continuous verification

title: Safe-state registry and containment rehearsal
thesis: Define the safe state for each use case and dependency before execution, then rehearse containment and recovery under realistic failure and adversarial conditions with evidence and limitations.
workflow: Define safe state, protected functions, and unacceptable stop effects
Map scoped containment mechanisms and dependencies
Run tabletop, simulation, and live non-production drill
Record reachability, latency, residual exposure, and recovery
metrics: use cases with tested safe state
risks: stop everything causes harm—scoped safe state
tabletop called proof—separate evidence tiers
safe state goes stale—material-change review

title: Scoped containment and graceful degradation
thesis: Contain by tenant, agent, warrant, capability, destination, credential, model/artifact, region, or dependency while preserving essential safe operations and proving that direct paths do not remain.
workflow: Select incident scope from correlated evidence
Simulate affected workloads and protected functions
Execute layered revoke, route, credential, process, and commit controls
Verify isolation and enter approved degraded mode
risks: scope incomplete—correlation and escape test
attacker alters control plane—out-of-band protected authority
graceful mode silently weakens evidence—explicit posture downgrade

title: Recovery orchestration and integrity verification
thesis: Restore identity, policy, credentials, data, queues, evidence, and agent execution in a controlled order; verify artifacts and state before reauthorization; and prevent recovery from replaying or duplicating external effects.
workflow: Select tested recovery plan and clean checkpoints
Verify artifacts, policy, identities, and custody
Restore dependencies in signed sequence
Re-run conformance and require owner reauthorization before consequence
risks: compromised backup restored—verify provenance
recovery races live system—fencing
staged effects replay—stable idempotency and boundary record

title: Purpose-bound context and data-rights envelope
thesis: Bind data origin, purpose, allowed transformations, recipients, retention, sensitivity, consent/legal basis reference, jurisdiction, and trust level to context so retrieval does not silently turn data into authority or memory.
workflow: Classify and label source at ingestion
Propagate rights and provenance through retrieval and transformation
Intersect use purpose with warrant and policy
Enforce at model context, memory, tool, and egress boundaries
risks: labels are untrusted—source authority and confidence
derived data loses restrictions—conservative propagation
policy too coarse blocks work—purpose templates and review

title: Provenance-aware memory admission and forgetting
thesis: Adopt origin-bound memory and transaction patterns so untrusted content cannot silently become durable instruction; require admission policy, provenance, expiry, user/owner visibility, correction, and deletion evidence.
workflow: Classify candidate memory by origin, purpose, and instruction risk
Evaluate write authority separately from read authority
Store with provenance, scope, expiry, and correction path
Re-evaluate on retrieval and prove expiry/deletion
risks: Warrantor reinvents memory store—stay at policy/evidence seam
deletion impossible in replicas—declare coverage
model summary hides origin—keep source links

title: Signed destination catalog and dynamic-egress approval
thesis: Operate a destination registry derived from approved capabilities, with verified service identity, path/method constraints, data-purpose compatibility, owner, expiry, and a human-approved workflow for genuinely dynamic destinations.
workflow: Resolve capability to catalog entry rather than agent hostname
Verify DNS/IP/TLS/service identity and path constraints
Inspect purpose/classification compatibility
Deny unknown target or route bounded discovery approval
risks: catalog becomes allowlist sprawl—owner and expiry
agent controls discovery result—out-of-band validation
SaaS endpoints change—provider-aware identity and health

title: Privacy, DLP, residency, and retention enforcement plane
thesis: Compose customer data classification, DLP, privacy, residency, retention, and data-subject controls with Warrantor purpose and action evidence, while keeping vendor detectors as advisory or defense-in-depth unless enforced by a protected boundary.
workflow: Ingest customer classifications and regulatory zones
Compile routing, storage, egress, redaction, and retention policy
Evaluate at context/tool/egress/commit boundaries
Record data lineage, decision, and exceptions
risks: detector called guarantee—state mode
redaction destroys utility—quality counter-metric
regimes conflict—deny or explicit counsel-approved exception

title: Unified verifiable evidence graph
thesis: Link principals, agents, manifests, warrants, policies, actions, receipts, effects, artifacts, controls, outcomes, findings, exceptions, incidents, and custody into a queryable graph while preserving canonical signed objects as the source of truth.
workflow: Verify and ingest canonical evidence
Resolve typed relationships without rewriting signed payload
Compute completeness, freshness, contradictions, and access projections
Serve population queries and drill back to raw proof
risks: graph becomes new truth—raw object remains authoritative
link inference is wrong—record source/confidence
cross-tenant leakage—tenant isolation and projection tests

title: Independent verifier SDK and portable assurance pack
thesis: Let a third party verify signatures, chain, policy freshness, artifact identity, enforcement mode, custody, population definition, sampled records, limitations, and unsupported claims without trusting Warrantor SaaS or sharing a secret.
workflow: Export canonical pack with manifest and verification instructions
Verify offline or against independent roots
Recompute derived claims and sampling population
Record pass, fail, indeterminate, and limitation separately
risks: pack summary hides failures—raw and derived checks mandatory
verification needs network—offline path
root distribution becomes vendor lock—customer and federated roots

title: Evidence custody, retention, legal hold, and time assurance
thesis: Operate append-only custody across local, customer, cloud, and offline archives with retention classes, legal holds, encryption, access evidence, migration, integrity scans, and explicit time-anchoring options.
workflow: Classify receipt/evidence retention at creation
Replicate to approved immutable storage and anchor per policy
Apply hold, access, and disposition workflows
Continuously verify integrity and migrate formats with provenance
risks: hash chain confused with absolute time—state semantics
retention violates minimization—policy and deletion
format becomes unreadable—migration and verifier fixtures

title: Audience-specific evidence views and control projections
outcome: Reuse one proof across many decisions
thesis: Project canonical evidence into approver, SOC, auditor, customer, board, insurer, procurement, and regulator views with purpose-based access, source links, applicability, freshness, confidence, and visible gaps.
workflow: Choose audience, purpose, scope, population, and period
Apply versioned mapping and least-data projection
Verify every statement against canonical evidence
Export with unsupported, stale, contradictory, and redacted fields visible
risks: pretty report launders uncertainty—gaps cannot be suppressed
mapping becomes legal conclusion—applicability sign-off
over-disclosure—purpose-limited views

title: Continuous control monitoring and attestation calendar
thesis: Continuously evaluate ownership, manifest, policy, identity, connector, conformance, evidence, exception, retention, and outcome requirements, opening owned remediation when truth becomes stale or contradictory.
workflow: Schedule or event-trigger control tests
Collect signed facts from source systems
Evaluate control-specific criteria and evidence freshness
Route fail, indeterminate, drift, and overdue states to owner
risks: green score hides test gaps—indeterminate separate
continuous polling becomes cost—event plus risk cadence
owners game tests—independent sampling

title: Evidence freshness, contradiction, and claim-drift detector
thesis: Detect when documents, dashboards, policies, manifests, connector claims, model metrics, and evidence packs disagree with newer target-commit or external evidence, without automatically deciding which statement is true.
workflow: Register claim and its evidence/mechanism/scope
Watch source changes and expiry
Compare structured facts and mark contradictions
Route investigation, correction, retraction, or accepted divergence
risks: text model invents contradiction—fact extraction needs review
older history is erased—retain supersession links
tool becomes censorship—show evidence and decision trail

title: Exception, waiver, and compensating-control lifecycle
thesis: Make every deviation scoped, owned, justified, risk-accepted, compensated, evidenced, approved, time-bounded, monitored, and automatically returned for closure or renewal without silent roll-forward.
workflow: Request exception against a specific control and resource
Assess consequence and compensating controls
Collect authorized approval and expiry
Monitor conditions, block silent renewal, and capture closure/root fix
risks: exception becomes permanent—hard expiry
broad scope—canonical resources and maximum consequence
renewal by same requester—SoD and escalation

title: Control-effectiveness sampling and outcome correlation
thesis: Combine population-aware evidence sampling, bypass/incident results, false-denial friction, exceptions, and business outcomes to estimate whether a control operates and is worth its burden—without treating correlation as causal proof.
workflow: Define population, expected operation, and counter-metrics
Select reproducible risk-based and random samples
Verify raw proof and exceptions
Record conclusion, uncertainty, action, and next experiment
risks: biased sampling—reproducible method
metric optimization—counter-metrics
causality overclaim—prospective experiments where material

title: Invariant attack corpus and capability elicitation
thesis: Maintain one evolving adversarial suite per invariant and action class, run with a capable attacker under substantiated elicitation, separating prevented, detected-not-prevented, violated, indeterminate, and untested.
workflow: Map invariant to attack goals and target topology
Elicit relevant capability and record substantiation
Run reproducible vectors and adaptive attacks
Sign report with limitations and add verified failures to regression
risks: zero violations sold as secure—coverage and limitations
benchmark overfit—private/adaptive cases
test harms systems—isolated targets and safety review

title: Human-approved attack-to-policy loop
outcome: Faster conversion of findings into protection
thesis: Turn a reproduced attack into a narrow candidate rule, regression case, impact simulation, shadow rollout, human approval, enforced change, and post-deployment outcome review.
workflow: Verify finding and affected scope
Generate or author the narrowest candidate control
Run regression, overbreadth, and business-impact tests
Approve shadow/canary/enforce/rollback and close with evidence
risks: automatic self-modification—human approval mandatory
rule broader than evidence—scope comparison
attack-specific patch misses class—regression family and review

title: External red-team and evaluator receipt adapters
thesis: Wrap garak, PyRIT, Inspect, AgentDojo, METR-style tasks, and approved sector tools; preserve their native artifacts; and sign run configuration, target, environment, dataset, evaluator, outcome, and limitation without claiming correctness.
workflow: Select approved evaluator and pin all artifacts
Run with declared topology, seeds, attempts, and grader
Preserve native outputs and normalize summary
Issue eval receipt and map to agent/control changes
risks: wrapper reimplements scanner—do not
score called truth—state semantics
grader drift—pin and cross-check
license/data restrictions—registry gate

title: Guard and evaluator integrity promotion gate
thesis: Require output-schema validity, severity vocabulary stability, slice floors, calibration, paired item analysis, false-positive limits, provenance, reproducibility, rollback, and human review before any advisory model is promoted.
workflow: Measure size/config-matched baseline with per-item outputs
Run candidate on frozen and adversarial sets
Compare schema, severity, categories, calibration, and paired outcomes
Return promote, refuse, or VOID with explicit human decision cases
risks: aggregate recall hides damage—multi-axis gates
candidate trained on test—leakage proof
model enters allow path—advisory can deny, never allow

title: Runtime-bound agent, tool, model, and data bill of materials
thesis: Bind the declared manifest and software/ML/data/tool inventory to the digests and versions that actually served each governed action, showing declared-versus-observed drift and unverified dependencies.
workflow: Generate signed declared BOM at build/onboarding
Capture runtime artifact and connector identities
Compare declared with served and policy
Bind relevant digest set into W2 evidence and open drift
risks: name/version accepted as identity—digest required
BOM is stale—runtime comparison
huge BOM inflates receipts—Merkle/reference with proof

title: Artifact verification, quarantine, and admission
thesis: Verify model, tool, skill, prompt pack, policy, container, dataset, and connector artifacts against signatures, provenance, allow/deny policy, vulnerability/license state, and runtime attestation before admission.
workflow: Resolve artifact by digest and collect provenance
Verify signature/root and policy requirements
Quarantine unknown or failed artifact and route exception
Admit exact digest and bind decision to runtime
risks: Warrantor rebuilds scanners/signing—integrate
fresh vulnerability appears after admission—continuous re-evaluation
mutable tags—digest pin

title: Agent and tool procurement assurance workflow
thesis: Assess an agent, tool, MCP server, model service, or workflow before purchase and encode the approved scope into manifests, policy, destinations, data rights, tests, and renewal monitoring so questionnaire answers become operational controls.
workflow: Collect vendor evidence and import technical manifest
Run sandbox/conformance/security/privacy tests
Define approved use cases, data, actions, destinations, and residual risk
Issue bounded onboarding decision and monitor renewal facts
risks: vendor claims trusted—behavioral tests
procurement approval treated as runtime authority—compile scope
assessment becomes stale—continuous monitoring and expiry

title: Dependency, vulnerability, license, and provenance policy
thesis: Combine customer-approved SCA, SBOM, vulnerability, exploitability, license, model/dataset terms, provenance, and maintenance signals into admission and continuous-use decisions with exception and rollback paths.
workflow: Ingest signed or attributable supply-chain signals
Evaluate use-case and consequence-specific policy
Block/quarantine/allow-with-exception
Re-evaluate on new evidence and trace affected governed actions
risks: CVSS alone drives action—include reachability and consequence
feed outage becomes false green—freshness
license interpretation automated—legal decision workflow

title: Agent incident cockpit and scoped stop
thesis: Provide one response surface for alerts, refused actions, anomalies, identity/policy/artifact changes, affected warrants, dependencies, active effects, containment options, safe-state status, custody, and recovery decisions.
workflow: Open or correlate incident from signed signals
Establish scope, consequence, and evidence confidence
Preview and authorize containment
Execute, verify, preserve custody, communicate, and recover
risks: dashboard becomes SIEM replacement—integrate and focus on agent action
broad stop causes harm—scoped safe-state preview
untrusted agent evidence—source confidence and external signals

title: Evidence timeline, correlation, and custody bridge
thesis: Correlate Warrantor receipts with OCSF/SIEM, OpenTelemetry, identity, endpoint, cloud, SaaS, and ticketing events while preserving the difference between operational telemetry and signed evidence.
workflow: Ingest signed receipts and referenced telemetry
Normalize time, identity, resource, and action correlations
Show source, confidence, gaps, and clock uncertainty
Preserve/export relevant artifacts under custody
risks: correlation becomes fact—show confidence
clock order mistaken for causal order—time uncertainty
duplicate data costs—reference rather than copy where possible

title: Emergency warrants and crisis approval
thesis: Provide narrowly scoped break-glass authority for containment and recovery with stronger identity, non-delegable quorum, explicit blast cap, shorter lifetime, dedicated evidence, and mandatory post-event review.
workflow: Declare incident and emergency objective
Compute bounded emergency capability and required quorum
Issue hardware-bound short-lived warrant
Execute only response actions, revoke, and require retrospective
risks: break-glass becomes routine—rare-use alerts and executive review
too broad—independent blast caps
compromised control plane—out-of-band protected issuance

title: Post-incident regression and value-impact closure
thesis: Require every confirmed incident to link affected outcomes and cost, root control gap, regression case, candidate policy/template change, owner, due date, and evidence that the fix works without unacceptable business friction.
workflow: Confirm incident facts and affected work/outcomes
Quantify exposure, response cost, and customer/business impact
Create regression and candidate control
Validate, deploy, and close with effectiveness and counter-metrics
risks: blame replaces learning—focus on control/system
impact is invented—finance/customer validation
closure on code merge—require operational evidence

title: Business-operator job launcher and live run
thesis: Let a non-technical operator launch pre-bounded templates, understand inputs and consequences, see live state and refusals, stop safely, handle requested decisions, and confirm the business outcome without authoring controls.
workflow: Choose approved template and provide validated inputs
Preview scope, cost, data use, and expected outcome
Run with live status, holds, and safe stop
Review result, exceptions, and confirm outcome
risks: power hidden as simplicity—show consequence and posture
operator changes bounds—templates only
live view implies surveillance—purpose and least data

title: Governance studio for inventory, controls, and exceptions
thesis: Give risk and control owners a coherent workspace for agents, use cases, owners, classification, controls, policies, evidence, monitoring, exceptions, attestations, and retirement over the full lifecycle.
workflow: Scope portfolio and assign ownership
Apply risk and regional modules
Assign controls/evidence and approve lifecycle
Monitor drift, exceptions, outcomes, and retirement
risks: becomes generic GRC—stay tied to executable agent facts
single score hides gaps—factor views
data entry burden—import and reuse with accountability

title: Evidence explorer and sampling workspace
thesis: Let auditors and assurance users define a population, inspect completeness and contradictions, run deterministic or risk-based samples, verify canonical proof, annotate limitations, and export a reproducible workpaper.
workflow: Define scope, period, population, and control question
Run query with stable snapshot
Select reproducible sample and verify raw evidence
Record findings, limitations, and conclusion; export workpaper
risks: tool guides desired conclusion—transparent query/sample
export loses interactive gaps—embed manifest
auditor access overbroad—purpose and scope

title: Executive autonomy and outcome command center
thesis: Show where autonomous work creates accepted outcomes, where oversight and control debt accumulate, where incidents and costs concentrate, and which use cases should expand, narrow, pause, or retire—with traceable drill-down.
workflow: Select portfolio lens and baseline period
Review autonomy, outcome, cost, risk, and evidence dimensions
Drill into uncertainty, negative outcomes, and control debt
Record funding/scope decision and next proof gate
risks: vanity dashboard—decision workflow required
risk color oversimplifies—multi-dimensional
ROI overclaim—confidence and counter-metrics

title: Connector SDK, capability mapping, and conformance contract
thesis: Give partners one typed way to declare operations, resources, constraints, identities, commit behavior, idempotency, staging, errors, versions, and coverage—with generated tests and an explicit enforced/mediated/observed map.
workflow: Define connector manifest and canonical mappings
Implement authorize/stage/perform/attest hooks
Run golden, adversarial, failure, and version tests
Publish signed coverage and support tier
risks: SDK owns security decision—thin adapters only
coverage self-asserted—tests and attestation
generic abstraction drops vendor constraint—fail unknown

title: Integration health and upstream-version laboratory
thesis: Continuously test connectors against supported and emerging upstream versions, auth changes, schemas, rate limits, failure modes, and security advisories; downgrade coverage and notify owners before production drift becomes silent bypass.
workflow: Maintain support matrix and reproducible fixtures
Run scheduled and change-triggered contract/failure tests
Compare behavior and coverage with prior verified release
Block, canary, downgrade, or retire with owner workflow
risks: lab differs from production—canary and customer facts
test cost explodes—support tiers by use
unknown version assumed compatible—default downgrade

title: Provider-neutral policy, manifest, decision, and evidence APIs
thesis: Expose stable, rate-limited, tenant-scoped APIs and SDKs for registry, authorize, attest, verify, contain, policy compile, evidence query, outcome accept, and administration with structured validation and idempotency.
workflow: Authenticate human/workload and tenant
Validate structured request at boundary
Execute narrow service operation with idempotency and rate policy
Return structured result, evidence reference, degradation, and retry semantics
risks: API becomes remote-only availability dependency—sidecar/in-process core path
hardcoded model/provider—provider abstraction
unbounded public endpoint—rate limit and quotas

title: Local developer, test, and deploy golden path
thesis: Provide one supported path to initialize a project, declare an agent, run mock and real local dependencies, exercise conformance, preview policy, issue/verify a receipt, deploy a reference topology, and understand what is not production-ready.
workflow: Initialize from typed template
Run local services and first receipt
Execute unit, integration, conformance, and escape tests
Generate deployment plan with required external services and posture
risks: mock success called production—loud posture
tooling sprawl—one canonical path
package names unowned—publication and provenance gate

title: Regional policy and evidence-pack framework
thesis: Define one signed package format for official sources, applicability prompts, control mappings, policy modules, evidence queries, retention/residency settings, languages, owners, version dates, update SLA, and unsupported gaps.
workflow: Select authoritative source and version
Map applicability and required technical facts
Review policy/evidence projections locally
Sign, publish, monitor changes, deprecate, and migrate
risks: legal advice implied—customer/counsel decision
weak web source—official primary gate
regional fork—stable module interface

title: Sovereign, air-gapped, and disconnected-edge operations
thesis: Deliver install, identity, key ceremony, offline update, artifact admission, policy distribution, evidence custody, verification, backup, support, and revocation/reconciliation for no-egress and intermittently connected environments.
workflow: Build signed offline bundle with manifest and dependencies
Install with local roots and customer-owned keys
Operate, verify, update, and contain without vendor network
Reconcile approved facts when connection returns without widening trust
risks: sovereign becomes bespoke fork—declarative topology
vendor dependency remains—offline verifier/export
stale security updates—signed update cadence and risk

title: Bilingual and culturally localized governance evidence UX
outcome: Adoption across GCC and global teams
thesis: Support Arabic/English and other required language views for business purpose, scope, approvals, exceptions, evidence packs, and regulatory mappings while keeping canonical policy identifiers and signed data language-neutral.
workflow: Store canonical structured facts and controlled terminology
Render localized human views with source-language links
Review high-consequence translations by qualified owner
Bind rendered version to canonical digest and preserve language used at approval
risks: translation changes policy meaning—canonical IDs and review
machine translation trusted—human gate where material
RTL treated as cosmetic—full usability test

title: Crypto-agility, customer roots, and key-ceremony operations
thesis: Support customer-managed and hardware-bound keys, M-of-N root issuance, rotation, dual-algorithm migration, compromise response, trust-bundle distribution, and independently witnessed ceremonies without making Warrantor a general PKI.
workflow: Choose approved algorithms, roots, HSM/KMS, quorum, and blast caps
Run witnessed generation/rotation ceremony
Distribute trust bundles and dual-sign during migration
Exercise compromise, revoke, recover, and verify historical evidence
risks: complexity causes outage—rehearsed rotation
root quorum centralizes control—customer governance
PQC marketing outruns support—only claim tested algorithms and profiles

title: Independent verifier and assurance-partner network
thesis: Enable auditors, assessors, incident firms, integrators, customer security teams, and research labs to verify Warrantor artifacts, publish scoped opinions, and contribute profiles under transparent governance.
workflow: Qualify partner and verifier implementation
Run public and private conformance
Issue scoped capability listing with expiry
Accept reports, revoke status, and resolve conflicts transparently
risks: pay-to-pass—separate fees from verdict
certification capture—multi-stakeholder governance
one verifier dominates—diversity metric

title: Conformance laboratory and expiring certification
thesis: Offer reproducible self-test, hosted, private, and accredited lab workflows for protocol, connector, invariant, containment, and deployment profiles with capability elicitation, visible limitations, version scope, and expiry.
workflow: Select profile, target, topology, and version
Run vectors, corpus, escape, and failure suites
Review evidence and limitations independently
Publish scoped result that expires on time, version, or material change
risks: certification mistaken for universal security—scope and expiry
vendor optimizes public corpus—private/adaptive tests
commercial pressure hides failure—immutable publication rules

title: Open profile governance and upstream contribution
thesis: Track agent identity, authorization, receipts, MCP, telemetry, findings, supply chain, policy, and containment standards; adopt overlapping work; contribute narrow profiles, vectors, and evidence semantics where Warrantor has implementation proof.
workflow: Maintain feature/date-aware overlap ledger
Select adopt, profile, contribute, or retire decision
Prototype against upstream and submit interoperable artifacts
Align product roadmap and migrate away from duplication
metrics: time from standard change to support
risks: novelty narrative resists adoption—outcome differentiation
draft treated as stable—status labels
standards work consumes build capacity—evidence-gated scope

title: Verified connector and solution marketplace
thesis: Publish searchable, signed listings for connectors, templates, policy packs, deployment blueprints, verifiers, and managed services only after conformance, ownership, support, security, and update obligations are mature.
workflow: Submit signed package and support metadata
Run security/conformance and licensing review
Publish scoped compatibility and customer-owned deployment path
Monitor versions, incidents, usage, disputes, and expiry
risks: marketplace before demand—defer
pay-to-rank—objective transparent ordering
supply-chain risk—signed artifacts and continuous review

title: Design-partner value realization program
thesis: Run a disciplined pilot from agreed use case and baseline through governed deployment, adoption, evidence review, outcome acceptance, negative results, value decision, and reusable reference pattern.
workflow: Select use case with consequence and measurable baseline
Agree 30/60/90-day outcome and control plan
Deploy minimum coherent lifecycle and review weekly
Produce customer-owned value/evidence review and expand, narrow, or stop
risks: pilot is unpaid custom engineering—scope and reusable pattern
success criteria move—freeze baseline
negative result hidden—record and publish internally

title: Customer adoption, control-health, and value review
thesis: Give customer success and owners a shared operating view of onboarding, active governed use, template adoption, posture, exceptions, review friction, evidence requests, incidents, outcomes, and next-best operational actions.
workflow: Establish adoption and value plan
Monitor use, health, evidence, and outcome signals
Route technical, governance, or change-management action
Run periodic value review with signed decisions and owners
risks: health score becomes opaque—show factors
usage surveillance—contractual purpose and aggregation
CS incentives hide risk—negative signals and independent risk view

title: Value-aligned packaging, metering, and entitlement
thesis: Meter managed assurance, governed agents/use cases, evidence retention and queries, connectors, regions, policy targets, conformance operations, and support—without closing the verifier, charging per denial, or making evidence hostage.
workflow: Define entitlement and value-aligned meters
Bind usage to tenant/work unit with privacy limits
Forecast and enforce spend/limits with clear degradation
Reconcile invoice, value, SLA, and dispute evidence
risks: meter incentives distort control—never price denies/incidents
evidence lock-in—portable export
complex pricing slows sales—few outcome-aligned units

title: Procurement, insurer, and capital assurance exchange
thesis: With explicit customer consent, let buyers, insurers, lenders, boards, and partners request narrowly scoped, independently verifiable evidence packages or continuous attestations—only after privacy, governance, demand, and anti-discrimination gates are proven.
workflow: Requester states purpose, evidence need, period, and decision
Customer approves least-data projection
Warrantor generates and verifier checks portable pack
Record use, decision, dispute, expiry, and revoke ongoing access
risks: score becomes discriminatory gate—no universal risk score
customer loses control—per-request consent and expiry
network begins before trust—defer until independent governance and demand

title: Tenant isolation and delegated customer administration
thesis: Separate identity, policy, evidence, keys, connectors, billing, support, and data by tenant and organizational boundary while allowing customers to delegate administration without granting platform-wide authority.
workflow: Provision tenant with customer-selected root and regions
Delegate scoped administration and enforce SoD
Continuously test data, cache, queue, log, and support isolation
Export, suspend, transfer, or delete tenant under verified lifecycle
risks: tenant ID checked only in UI—enforce at storage and service boundaries
support becomes superuser—just-in-time witnessed access
shared caches leak—partition and adversarial tests

title: Reliability, capacity, backpressure, and rate-limit control
thesis: Define and enforce tenant, agent, connector, evidence, reviewer-queue, and control-plane capacity so overload cannot create uncontrolled retry, spend, duplicate effects, missing evidence, or silent fail-open behavior.
workflow: Declare SLO, quota, retry, concurrency, queue, and degradation policy
Measure capacity by consequence and topology
Apply idempotent backpressure and safe shedding
Reconcile delayed work, evidence, and customer impact
risks: routine work starves critical response—priority isolation
rate limit bypass through connectors—shared work-unit budget
degradation hides weakened posture—explicit mode and alert

title: Environment, secret, and configuration governance
thesis: Inventory and attest environment variables, connector credentials, policy references, feature flags, endpoints, trust bundles, and deployment parameters that materially affect authority or evidence, without exposing secret values.
workflow: Classify security- and claim-relevant configuration
Bind secret references and configuration digests to deployment
Detect drift, unknown defaults, and unsupported combinations
Rotate, roll back, or reauthorize with signed change evidence
risks: secret values leak into evidence—references only
default changes silently—explicit versioned configuration
hash proves bytes not safety—policy and conformance checks

title: Change, release, canary, rollback, and compatibility governance
thesis: Treat agent, model, prompt, tool, connector, policy, manifest, schema, and platform changes as governed releases with impact analysis, evidence gates, canaries, rollback, and customer compatibility windows.
workflow: Classify material change and affected governed objects
Run contract, security, performance, outcome, and migration gates
Canary by tenant/use case with rollback thresholds
Promote, hold, revert, communicate, and preserve evidence
risks: calendar deadline overrides evidence—gate-based promotion
rollback cannot reverse external effects—separate platform and business recovery
long compatibility tail—published windows and migration tools

title: Customer trust center and live assurance portal
thesis: Provide customer-scoped access to architecture, security posture, subprocessor and deployment facts, control/evidence mappings, incident communications, conformance, availability, privacy, and portable proof with freshness and unsupported gaps.
workflow: Authenticate requester and record assurance purpose
Select customer/edition/deployment-specific facts
Verify freshness and produce least-data view
Answer questions, record reliance, export evidence, and expire access
risks: generic trust page overclaims customer topology—scoped view
security details exposed—purpose and least privilege
marketing edits bypass claim review—evidence-derived content

title: Role competency, training, and authorization assurance
thesis: Define the knowledge and rehearsal required for operators, approvers, security responders, auditors, policy authors, and administrators; bind completion and recency to authority for high-consequence actions.
workflow: Define competency by role and consequence
Deliver scenario-based training and safe-state drills
Assess comprehension and practical decision quality
Issue time-bounded role authorization and trigger retraining on change/incident
risks: training completion mistaken for competence—practical assessment
worker surveillance—use only role assurance
authorization blocks emergency response—break-glass with retrospective

title: Approval quality, cognitive load, and automation-bias controls
thesis: Measure whether reviewers understand consequences, inspect evidence, disagree appropriately, and remain within cognitive and queue limits; redesign routing and presentation before adding more automated recommendations.
workflow: Define decision-quality and workload signals with worker participation
Sample comprehension, reversals, reasons, overrides, and queue conditions
Identify fatigue, concentration, bias, and misleading UI
Change routing/interface/policy and remeasure
risks: metric becomes employee performance score—prohibit individual ranking
reviewers game reason codes—sampling and qualitative review
AI suggestions anchor decisions—blind comparison and influence audit

title: Guided onboarding, contextual help, and support evidence
thesis: Embed role-aware explanation, safe examples, diagnostic checks, status semantics, and support escalation into every critical workflow while capturing enough evidence to reproduce problems without exporting sensitive content by default.
workflow: Detect workflow and current governed context
Offer task-specific explanation and preflight checks
Collect consented diagnostic bundle with redaction
Resolve, document, and turn recurring issues into product or control fixes
risks: help hides consequence—never replace scope preview
diagnostics leak data—redaction and preview
support workaround becomes permanent—exception and root-fix workflow

title: Financial transaction and payment authority profile
thesis: Define payee, account, amount, currency, purpose, cumulative and velocity limits, sanctions/fraud signals, SoD, non-delegable approval, idempotency, settlement state, reversal limits, and reconciliation for financial actions.
workflow: Resolve canonical payee/account and purpose
Intersect transaction, daily, vendor, and delegated limits
Run deterministic controls and advisory fraud signals
Obtain required approval, stage/commit idempotently, and reconcile settlement
risks: fraud model authorizes—advisory may deny only
idempotency fails across provider—stable external key
compensation assumed—state actual reversal capability

title: Cyber-physical and robotics safe-action profile
thesis: Extend action, authority, evidence, containment, and safe-state semantics to physical actuation, location, machine state, human proximity, interlocks, command acknowledgment, and recovery only with sector experts and hardware-enforced boundaries.
workflow: Define physical hazard and known-safe state
Bind device/workload identity and hardware interlocks
Require simulation, test cell, staged authority, and non-delegable approval
Execute, verify physical acknowledgment, monitor, contain, and recover
metrics: containment latency and false stop harm
risks: software receipt cannot prove physics—sensor/hardware evidence and limitation
generic platform overreaches—defer and partner
network stop is unsafe—local independent safe state

title: Data-subject rights, notice, appeal, and contestability workflow
thesis: Link affected-person notice, data provenance, purpose, automated contribution, human review, correction, deletion, appeal, and remedy to governed actions where agents influence people or personal-data decisions.
workflow: Identify rights-triggering use case and affected records
Generate accurate notice and access package from evidence
Route correction, deletion, human review, or appeal with deadline
Record decision, downstream propagation, remedy, and closure
risks: evidence exposes others—redacted scoped view
automated explanation invented—fact-derived plus human review
deletion conflicts with legal hold—explicit counsel decision

title: Accessibility, assistive technology, and inclusive decision design
thesis: Make all operator, approval, incident, evidence, and governance workflows usable with keyboard, screen reader, magnification, high contrast, reduced motion, accessible documents, clear language, and alternative notification modes.
workflow: Define WCAG-aligned requirements and critical-task journeys
Test semantic structure, focus, contrast, reflow, documents, and time limits
Include disabled users in decision-comprehension studies
Block release on critical barriers and record exceptions with expiry
risks: automated scan called compliance—manual task testing
time-bound approvals disadvantage users—accessible extensions and routing
visual color carries truth alone—text and structure
